jp: 今日[きょう]は遅[おく]れてすみません。電車[でんしゃ]が止[と]まった{んです|pt-nda}。
en: Sorry I'm late today. You see, the train stopped.
why: Giving the reason for being late in your own words takes んです.

jp: 顔色[かおいろ]が悪[わる]いですね。どうした{んですか|pt-nda}。
en: You look pale. What's the matter?
why: Asking the reason behind something you can see calls for んですか.

jp: すみません、頭[あたま]が痛[いた]い{んです|pt-nda}。今日[きょう]は休[やす]ませてください。
en: I'm sorry, my head hurts. Please let me take today off.
why: The speaker explains their own condition as the reason for a request.

jp: どうして泣[な]いている{んですか|pt-nda}。何[なに]かあったんですか。
en: Why are you crying? Did something happen?
why: A why-question about a visible situation asks for an explanation, so んですか.

jp: 父[ちち]は今[いま]、出張[しゅっちょう]で大阪[おおさか]に行[い]っている{んです|pt-nda}。
en: My father is away on a business trip in Osaka right now (that's why he isn't here).
why: Explaining why the father is not here, in the speaker's own words, takes んです.

jp: ごめん、今夜[こんや]は行[い]けない。明日[あした]試験[しけん]がある{んだ|pt-nda}。
en: Sorry, I can't go tonight. I have an exam tomorrow.
why: The plain form of んです gives the speaker's own reason.

jp: どうしてそんなに急[いそ]いでいる{の|pt-nda}。
en: Why are you in such a hurry? (casual)
why: The casual question form の asks the reason for something you see.

jp: あの、ちょっとお願[ねが]いがある{んですが|pt-nda}。
en: Um, I have a small favour to ask.
why: んですが introduces the background before a request.

jp: 日本語[にほんご]が上手[じょうず]ですね。どこで勉強[べんきょう]した{んですか|pt-nda}。
en: Your Japanese is good. Where did you study it?
why: Asking for the story behind something you notice calls for んですか.

jp: 財布[さいふ]を忘[わす]れた{んです|pt-nda}。お金[かね]を貸[か]してくれませんか。
en: I forgot my wallet. Could you lend me some money?
why: The speaker explains why they need to borrow money.

jp: 昨日[きのう]は学校[がっこう]を休[やす]んだ。熱[ねつ]があった{のだ/んだ|pt-nda}。
en: I stayed home from school yesterday. I had a fever.
why: A plain-style explanation of one's own reason takes のだ.

jp: おなかがすいた{んです|pt-nda}。何[なに]か食[た]べてもいいですか。
en: I'm hungry. May I eat something?
why: Giving one's own feeling as the reason for asking permission takes んです.

jp: 駅[えき]までどうやって行[い]った{んですか|pt-nda}。
en: How did you get to the station?
why: A question about the means of something that already happened takes んですか.

jp: そのかばんはどこで買[か]った{んですか|pt-nda}。素敵[すてき]ですね。
en: Where did you buy that bag? It's lovely.
why: Showing interest in something you see and asking for details uses んですか.

jp: 今日[きょう]は仕事[しごと]が早[はや]く終[お]わった{んだ|pt-nda}。だから、一緒[いっしょ]に晩[ばん]ご飯[はん]を食[た]べよう。
en: My work finished early today. So let's have dinner together.
why: The plain explanation gives the reason for the invitation that follows.

jp: 彼[かれ]は来[こ]なかった。約束[やくそく]を忘[わす]れていた{のだ/んだ|pt-nda}。
en: He didn't come. The reason was that he had forgotten the appointment.
why: The second sentence explains the reason behind the first, which のだ marks.

jp: すみません、少[すこ]し寒[さむ]い{んです|pt-nda}。窓[まど]を閉[し]めてもいいですか。
en: I'm sorry, I'm a little cold. May I close the window?
why: The speaker's own sensation is the reason for the request.

jp: どうして日本語[にほんご]を勉強[べんきょう]している{んですか|pt-nda}。
en: Why are you studying Japanese?
why: Asking for someone's reason takes んですか.

jp: 母[はは]に怒[おこ]られた。宿題[しゅくだい]をしなかった{んだ|pt-nda}。
en: I was scolded by my mother. I hadn't done my homework.
why: The plain explanation tells why the speaker was scolded.

jp: 実[じつ]は来週[らいしゅう]、誕生日[たんじょうび]{なんです|pt-nda}。
en: Actually, my birthday is next week.
why: Telling someone a fact about yourself that they didn't know uses なんです.

jp: 電話[でんわ]に出[で]られなくてすみません。会議中[かいぎちゅう]だった{んです|pt-nda}。
en: Sorry I couldn't answer the phone. I was in a meeting.
why: The speaker explains, from their own knowledge, why they missed the call.

jp: 元気[げんき]がありませんね。何[なに]か心配[しんぱい]なことがある{んですか|pt-nda}。
en: You seem down. Is something worrying you?
why: Noticing someone's mood and asking for the cause takes んですか.

jp: もう帰[かえ]ります。明日[あした]は朝[あさ]早[はや]い{んです|pt-nda}。
en: I'm going home now. I have to get up early tomorrow.
why: Giving one's own reason for leaving takes んです.

jp: ごめん、今[いま]忙[いそが]しい{んだ|pt-nda}。あとで電話[でんわ]するね。
en: Sorry, I'm busy at the moment. I'll call you later.
why: The speaker gives their own reason for not talking now.

jp: テレビをつけてもいいですか。見[み]たい番組[ばんぐみ]がある{んです|pt-nda}。
en: May I turn on the TV? There's a programme I want to watch.
why: The reason behind the request is the speaker's own, so んです.

jp: どうして窓[まど]を開[あ]けた{んですか|pt-nda}。寒[さむ]いですよ。
en: Why did you open the window? It's cold!
why: Asking the reason for an action that has just surprised the speaker takes んですか.

jp: 私[わたし]はお酒[さけ]が飲[の]めません。体[からだ]に合[あ]わない{んです|pt-nda}。
en: I can't drink alcohol. It doesn't agree with me.
why: The speaker explains their own condition as the reason.

jp: 昨日[きのう]は何[なに]も食[た]べなかった。食欲[しょくよく]がなかった{のだ/んだ|pt-nda}。
en: I ate nothing yesterday. I had no appetite.
why: The reason behind the previous fact is stated in the plain written style.

jp: 外[そと]がにぎやかですね。どうしてみんな笑[わら]っている{んですか|pt-nda}。
en: It's lively outside. Why is everyone laughing?
why: A why-question about something happening in front of the speaker takes んですか.

jp: すみません、傘[かさ]を持[も]っていない{んです|pt-nda}。入[い]れてもらえませんか。
en: Excuse me, I don't have an umbrella. Could I share yours?
why: Explaining one's situation as the reason for asking a favour.

jp: 先月[せんげつ]から、駅[えき]の近[ちか]くの店[みせ]で働[はたら]いている{んです|pt-nda}。
en: I've been working at a shop near the station since last month.
why: Offering new information about oneself in an explaining tone takes んです.

jp: どこへ行[い]く{んですか|pt-nda}。もうすぐ雨[あめ]が降[ふ]りますよ。
en: Where are you going? It's about to rain, you know.
why: Asking about the plan behind what you see the other person doing takes んですか.

jp: このカレーは辛[から]すぎる。子[こ]どもは食[た]べられない{んだ|pt-nda}。
en: This curry is too spicy. The children can't eat it.
why: The speaker explains in plain style why the curry is a problem.

jp: 先生[せんせい]、質問[しつもん]がある{んですが|pt-nda}、今[いま]よろしいですか。
en: Teacher, I have a question; is now a good time?
why: んですが sets the scene before a question or request.

jp: 昨日[きのう]、鍵[かぎ]を落[お]とした{んです|pt-nda}。それで交番[こうばん]に行[い]きました。
en: I lost my keys yesterday. So I went to the police box.
why: The speaker explains what happened as the background to the next fact.

jp: 今日[きょう]は運動[うんどう]しない。足[あし]が痛[いた]い{んだ|pt-nda}。
en: I'm not exercising today. My leg hurts.
why: The speaker gives their own reason for skipping exercise.

jp: 日本[にほん]の夏[なつ]は苦手[にがて]です。暑[あつ]くて、すぐ疲[つか]れてしまう{んです|pt-nda}。
en: I don't cope well with Japanese summers. It's so hot that I get tired quickly.
why: The speaker explains how the heat affects them every year.

jp: さっきから何[なに]を探[さが]している{んですか|pt-nda}。手伝[てつだ]いましょうか。
en: What have you been looking for all this time? Shall I help?
why: The speaker has noticed the search and asks for the explanation, so んですか.

jp: 雨[あめ]の日[ひ]は散歩[さんぽ]をしません。靴[くつ]がぬれる{のです/んです|pt-nda}。
en: I don't go for walks on rainy days. My shoes get wet.
why: のです gives the general reason behind a habit.

jp: 家[いえ]は駅[えき]から遠[とお]い{んです|pt-nda}。毎朝[まいあさ]三十分[さんじゅっぷん]歩[ある]いています。
en: My home is far from the station. I walk thirty minutes every morning.
why: The speaker explains the background of the daily walk.

jp: コートがぬれていますね。外[そと]は雪[ゆき]が降[ふ]っている{んですか|pt-nda}。
en: Your coat is wet. Is it snowing outside?
why: Asking to confirm the reason behind what you notice takes んですか.

jp: 今夜[こんや]のパーティーには行[い]けません。友達[ともだち]が来[く]る{んです|pt-nda}。
en: I can't go to tonight's party. A friend is coming over.
why: The speaker explains their own reason for declining.

jp: 今年[ことし]は旅行[りょこう]に行[い]かない。お金[かね]がない{んだ|pt-nda}。
en: I'm not travelling this year. I don't have any money.
why: Giving the plain-style reason for not travelling.

jp: いつも早[はや]く起[お]きますね。何時[なんじ]に寝[ね]る{んですか|pt-nda}。
en: You always get up early. What time do you go to bed?
why: Asking for a detail behind something noticed uses んですか.

jp: その本[ほん]を読[よ]んでみたい{んです|pt-nda}。貸[か]してくださいませんか。
en: I'd like to try reading that book. Could you lend it to me?
why: The speaker's own wish is given as the reason for the request.

jp: すみません、道[みち]がわからない{んです|pt-nda}。駅[えき]はどこですか。
en: Excuse me, I don't know the way. Where is the station?
why: The speaker explains their own situation before asking.
